newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-CHAOS AT MARACANA AS DIRECTORS INVADE PITCH TWICE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHAOS AT MARACANA AS DIRECTORS INVADE PITCH TWICE.

text.p: A Brazilian championship match at the Maracana stadium descended into total chaos on Sunday when directors from both clubs interrupted the Vasco da Gama-Botafogo game to protest refereeing decisions.
Play was delayed for more than 20 minutes when Eurico Miranda, a Vasco director and member of the Brazilian Congress, ran onto the pitch to protest about the goal which gave Botafogo a 1-0 lead.

Vasco turned the game around with two goals following the interruption but after their second goal the president of Botafogo, Carlos Alberto Montenegro, followed Miranda's example and rushed onto the field to remonstrate with the referee.
Touchline reporters said later that Miranda had threatened police who tried to usher him off the pitch, warning them that he enjoyed parliamentary immunity.
Montenegro said: "I told the referee that he was a coward and a failure."
Vasco claimed that Botafogo striker Tulio was offside when he headed in the first goal of the game, which Vasco eventually won 2-1.
Vasco coach Antonio Lopes was first onto the field, running straight towards referee Jorge Travassos, but he was followed by a horde of officials, police and radio reporters.

Lopes and Miranda were sent off after ten minutes of wrangling but Miranda then sat down on the Vasco substitutes' bench and refused police instrutcions to leave, holding up play for another 12 minutes.
After the re-start Ranielli equalised for Vasco from a free kick, then Edmundo scored the winner from what appeared to be an offside position, sparking Montenegro's protest.
Play was delayed for another five minutes with reporters, other officials and players once again joining in and police attempting to restore order.
Miranda, elected to Congress two years ago after a campaign directed almost exclusively at Vasco fans, said he had no regrets about his pitch invasion.
"It depends on the moment. Their goal was scandalous, a clear offside. You can't just let something like that pass," he said.
Montenegro was equally unrepentant. "They had five players offside," he fumed.
At the end of the game, there was more trouble as Botafogo players surrounded the match officials, who were led off under police protection.
The win maintained Vasco's slight hopes of finishing in the top eight and reaching the quarter-finals of the championship, but virtually ended Botafogo's chances.

Palmeiras stayed top of the table after a 1-0 win over Flamengo, who were missing injured striker Romario. Cruzeiro remained second after a 2-1 win over Atletico Mineiro in a derby match in Belo Horizonte, watched by an 87,000 crowd.
Sao Paulo, who sacked Brazil's 1994 World Cup winning coach Carlos Alberto Parreira on Wednesday after a run of ten games without a win, beat Criciuma 5-3 under interim coach Muricy Ramalho.
